changes.after: Choose an object shape by checking its type.

before: T extends string ? A : B chooses a type, not a runtime branch. If the supplied type fits string, the result is A; otherwise it is B. This extends tests assignability, not class inheritance.

Stored<string> becomes {text:string}; Stored<number> becomes {value:number}. The ? and : separate true and false type branches. The values remain ordinary objects; there is no runtime Stored function and no automatic conversion of external input. The code prints Cloud and 6.
Optional local practice: Try Stored<boolean> with a value property and explain why text would be wrong.
after: A conditional type chooses one type or another. In `T extends string ? A : B`, extends asks whether T fits the string type. If it does, choose A; otherwise, choose B. This is a type check, not a running if statement.
For Stored, a string gets a text property. Other types get a value property. The question mark begins the first choice, and the colon begins the other choice.
Boolean means true or false. It does not fit string, so Stored<boolean> needs a value property holding a boolean.
Stored describes the required shape. It does not make the object or convert its data. You supply the actual object values.
